verses.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες Τίς ἄρα μείζων ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν
verses.transliteration: En ekeinē tē hōra prosēlthon hoi mathētai tō Iēsou legontes Tis ara meizōn estin en tē basileia tōn ouranōn
verses.literal: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven
verses.literalPt: Naquela hora, chegaram-se os discípulos a Jesus e perguntaram: Quem é, porventura, o maior no reino dos céus?

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai proskalesamenos paidion estēsen auto en mesō autōn
verses.literal: Jesus invited a little child to stand . . . among them
verses.literalPt: Jesus, chamando para junto de si um menino, pô-lo no meio deles

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἐὰν μὴ στραφῆτε καὶ γένησθε ὡς τὰ παιδία οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν
verses.transliteration: kai eipen Amēn legō hymin ean mē straphēte kai genēsthe hōs ta paidia ou mē eiselthēte eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn
verses.literal: Truly I tell you He said unless . . . you change and become like little children you will never enter . . . the kingdom of heaven
verses.literalPt: e disse: Em verdade vos digo que, se não vos converterdes e não vos fizerdes como meninos, de modo algum entrareis no reino dos céus.

verses.original: ὅστις οὖν ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὡς τὸ παιδίον τοῦτο οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ μείζων ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν
verses.transliteration: hostis oun tapeinōsei heauton hōs to paidion touto houtos estin ho meizōn en tē basileia tōn ouranōn
verses.literal: Therefore whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven
verses.literalPt: Quem, pois, se tornar humilde como este menino, esse será o maior no reino dos céus.

verses.original: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται ἓν παιδίον τοιοῦτο ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐμὲ δέχεται
verses.transliteration: kai hos ean dexētai hen paidion toiouto epi tō onomati mou eme dechetai
verses.literal: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me
verses.literalPt: Aquele que receber um menino, tal como este, em meu nome a mim é que recebe;

verses.original: Ὃς δ’ ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ συμφέρει αὐτῷ ἵνα κρεμασθῇ μύλος ὀνικὸς περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ καταποντισθῇ ἐν τῷ πελάγει τῆς θαλάσσης
verses.transliteration: Hos d’ an skandalisē hena tōn mikrōn toutōn tōn pisteuontōn eis eme sympherei autō hina kremasthē mylos onikos peri ton trachēlon autou kai katapontisthē en tō pelagei tēs thalassēs
verses.literal: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea
verses.literalPt: mas quem puser uma pedra de tropeço no caminho de um destes pequeninos que creem em mim, melhor seria que se lhe pendurasse ao pescoço uma grande pedra de moinho e que fosse lançado no fundo do mar.

verses.original: Οὐαὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ἀπὸ τῶν σκανδάλων ἀνάγκη γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τὰ σκάνδαλα πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ δι’ οὗ τὸ σκάνδαλον ἔρχεται
verses.transliteration: Ouai tō kosmō apo tōn skandalōn anankē gar elthein ta skandala plēn ouai tō anthrōpō di’ hou to skandalon erchetai
verses.literal: Woe to the world for the causes of sin These stumbling blocks must come but woe to the man through whom they come
verses.literalPt: Ai do mundo por causa dos tropeços! Porque é necessário que apareçam tropeços; mas ai do homem por quem vem o tropeço!

verses.original: Εἰ δὲ ἡ χείρ σου ἢ ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζει σε ἔκκοψον αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ καλόν σοί ἐστιν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν κυλλὸν ἢ χωλόν ἢ δύο χεῖρας ἢ δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον
verses.transliteration: Ei de hē cheir sou ē ho pous sou skandalizei se ekkopson auton kai bale apo sou kalon soi estin eiselthein eis tēn zōēn kyllon ē chōlon ē dyo cheiras ē dyo podas echonta blēthēnai eis to pyr to aiōnion
verses.literal: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin . . . cut it off . . . and throw it away . . . . . . It is better for you to enter . . . life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire
verses.literalPt: Se a tua mão ou o teu pé te serve de pedra de tropeço, corta-o e lança-o de ti; melhor é entrares na vida manco ou aleijado do que, tendo duas mãos ou dois pés, seres lançado no fogo eterno.

verses.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζει σε ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ καλόν σοί ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός
verses.transliteration: kai ei ho ophthalmos sou skandalizei se exele auton kai bale apo sou kalon soi estin monophthalmon eis tēn zōēn eiselthein ē dyo ophthalmous echonta blēthēnai eis tēn geennan tou pyros
verses.literal: And if your eye causes you to sin . . . gouge it out . . . and throw it away . . . . . . It is better for you to enter . . . life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell
verses.literalPt: Se o teu olho te serve de pedra de tropeço, arranca-o e lança-o de ti; melhor é entrares na vida com um só dos teus olhos do que, tendo dois, seres lançado na Geena de fogo.

verses.original: Ὁρᾶτε μὴ καταφρονήσητε ἑνὸς τῶν μικρῶν τούτων λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτῶν ἐν οὐρανοῖς διὰ παντὸς βλέπουσι τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς
verses.transliteration: Horate mē kataphronēsēte henos tōn mikrōn toutōn legō gar hymin hoti hoi angeloi autōn en ouranois dia pantos blepousi to prosōpon tou Patros mou tou en ouranois
verses.literal: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones For I tell you that their angels in heaven always . . . see the face of My Father in heaven
verses.literalPt: Vede, não desprezeis um destes pequeninos; porque vos digo que os seus anjos nos céus veem incessantemente a face de meu Pai celestial.
[Porque o Filho do homem veio salvar o que havia perecido.]

verses.original: Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ ἐὰν γένηταί τινι ἀνθρώπῳ ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ πλανηθῇ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐχὶ ἀφήσει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη καὶ πορευθεὶς ζητεῖ τὸ πλανώμενον
verses.transliteration: Ti hymin dokei ean genētai tini anthrōpō hekaton probata kai planēthē hen ex autōn ouchi aphēsei ta enenēkonta ennea epi ta orē kai poreutheis zētei to planōmenon
verses.literal: What do you think If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray will he not leave the ninety-nine . . . on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost
verses.literalPt: Que vos parece? Se um homem tiver cem ovelhas, e uma delas se extraviar, não deixa as noventa e nove e vai aos montes procurar a que se extraviou?

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν γένηται εὑρεῖν αὐτό ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι χαίρει ἐπ’ αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα τοῖς μὴ πεπλανημένοις
verses.transliteration: kai ean genētai heurein auto amēn legō hymin hoti chairei ep’ autō mallon ē epi tois enenēkonta ennea tois mē peplanēmenois
verses.literal: And if he finds it truly I tell you he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine . . . that did not go astray
verses.literalPt: Se acontecer achá-la, em verdade vos digo que se regozija mais por causa desta do que pelas noventa e nove que não se extraviaram.

verses.original: οὕτως οὐκ ἔστιν θέλημα ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μικρῶν τούτων
verses.transliteration: houtōs ouk estin thelēma emprosthen tou Patros hymōn tou en ouranois hina apolētai hen tōn mikrōn toutōn
verses.literal: In the same way your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish
verses.literalPt: Assim, não é da vontade de vosso Pai, que está nos céus, que pereça um destes pequeninos.

verses.original: Ἐὰν δὲ ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ ὁ ἀδελφός σου ὕπαγε ἔλεγξον αὐτὸν μεταξὺ σοῦ καὶ αὐτοῦ μόνου ἐάν σου ἀκούσῃ ἐκέρδησας τὸν ἀδελφόν σου
verses.transliteration: Ean de hamartēsē eis se ho adelphos sou hypage elenxon auton metaxy sou kai autou monou ean sou akousē ekerdēsas ton adelphon sou
verses.literal: If your brother sins against you go and confront him privately . . . . . . . . . . . . If he listens to you you have won your brother over
verses.literalPt: Se teu irmão pecar, vai repreendê-lo entre ti e ele só. Se ele te ouvir, ganhado terás teu irmão;

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀκούσῃ παράλαβε μετὰ σοῦ ἔτι ἕνα ἢ δύο ἵνα Ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων ἢ τριῶν σταθῇ πᾶν ῥῆμα
verses.transliteration: ean de mē akousē paralabe meta sou eti hena ē dyo hina Epi stomatos dyo martyrōn ē triōn stathē pan rhēma
verses.literal: But if he will not listen take one or two others along . . . so that every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses
verses.literalPt: mas, se não te ouvir, leva ainda contigo uma ou duas pessoas, para que, por boca de duas ou três testemunhas, toda questão fique decidida.

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ παρακούσῃ αὐτῶν εἰπὸν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐὰν δὲ καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας παρακούσῃ ἔστω σοι ὥσπερ ὁ ἐθνικὸς καὶ ὁ τελώνης
verses.transliteration: ean de parakousē autōn eipon tē ekklēsia ean de kai tēs ekklēsias parakousē estō soi hōsper ho ethnikos kai ho telōnēs
verses.literal: If he refuses to listen to them tell it to the church And if he refuses to listen even to the church regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector
verses.literalPt: Se ele recusar ouvi-los, dize-o à igreja; e, se também recusar ouvir a igreja, considera-o como gentio e publicano.

verses.original: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅσα ἐὰν δήσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ὅσα ἐὰν λύσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ
verses.transliteration: Amēn legō hymin hosa ean dēsēte epi tēs gēs estai dedemena en ouranō kai hosa ean lysēte epi tēs gēs estai lelymena en ouranō
verses.literal: Truly I tell you whatever . . . you bind on earth will be bound in heaven and whatever . . . you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven
verses.literalPt: Em verdade vos digo: Tudo o que ligardes sobre a terra será ligado no céu; e tudo o que desligardes sobre a terra será desligado no céu.

verses.original: Πάλιν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν δύο συμφωνήσωσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς περὶ παντὸς πράγματος οὗ ἐὰν αἰτήσωνται γενήσεται αὐτοῖς παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς
verses.transliteration: Palin amēn legō hymin hoti ean dyo symphōnēsōsin ex hymōn epi tēs gēs peri pantos pragmatos hou ean aitēsōntai genēsetai autois para tou Patros mou tou en ouranois
verses.literal: Again I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything . . . you ask for it will be done for you by My Father in heaven
verses.literalPt: Ainda vos digo mais que, se dois de vós sobre a terra concordarem em pedir alguma coisa, ser-lhes-á feita por meu Pai, que está nos céus.

verses.original: οὗ γάρ εἰσιν δύο ἢ τρεῖς συνηγμένοι εἰς τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα ἐκεῖ εἰμι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: hou gar eisin dyo ē treis synēgmenoi eis to emon onoma ekei eimi en mesō autōn
verses.literal: For where two or three gather together in My name there am I with them . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Pois, onde dois ou três estão congregados em meu nome, ali estou eu no meio deles.

verses.original: Τότε προσελθὼν ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Κύριε ποσάκις ἁμαρτήσει εἰς ἐμὲ ὁ ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀφήσω αὐτῷ ἕως ἑπτάκις
verses.transliteration: Tote proselthōn ho Petros eipen autō Kyrie posakis hamartēsei eis eme ho adelphos mou kai aphēsō autō heōs heptakis
verses.literal: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked Lord how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me Up to seven times
verses.literalPt: Então, Pedro, aproximando-se, lhe perguntou: Senhor, quantas vezes pecará meu irmão contra mim, que lhe hei de perdoar? Será até sete vezes?

verses.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐ λέγω σοι ἕως ἑπτάκις ἀλλὰ ἕως ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά
verses.transliteration: Legei autō ho Iēsous Ou legō soi heōs heptakis alla heōs hebdomēkontakis hepta
verses.literal: Jesus answered . . . I tell you not just seven times but seventy-seven times . . .
verses.literalPt: Respondeu-lhe Jesus: Não te digo que até sete vezes, mas até setenta vezes sete.

verses.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ ὃς ἠθέλησεν συνᾶραι λόγον μετὰ τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Dia touto hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō basilei hos ēthelēsen synarai logon meta tōn doulōn autou
verses.literal: Because of this the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants
verses.literalPt: Por isso, o reino dos céus é semelhante a um rei que resolveu ajustar contas com os seus servos.

verses.original: ἀρξαμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ συναίρειν προσηνέχθη εἷς αὐτῷ ὀφειλέτης μυρίων ταλάντων
verses.transliteration: arxamenou de autou synairein prosēnechthē heis autō opheiletēs myriōn talantōn
verses.literal: As he began the settlements a debtor owing ten thousand talents was brought to him
verses.literalPt: Tendo começado a ajustá-las, trouxeram-lhe um que lhe devia dez mil talentos.

verses.original: μὴ ἔχοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀποδοῦναι ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος πραθῆναι καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀποδοθῆναι
verses.transliteration: mē echontos de autou apodounai ekeleusen auton ho kyrios prathēnai kai tēn gynaika kai ta tekna kai panta hosa echei kai apodothēnai
verses.literal: Since the man was unable to pay the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt along with his wife and children and everything he owned
verses.literalPt: Não tendo, porém, o servo com que pagar, ordenou o seu senhor que fossem vendidos — ele, sua mulher, seus filhos e tudo quanto possuía, e que se pagasse a dívida.

verses.original: Πεσὼν οὖν ὁ δοῦλος προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων Μακροθύμησον ἐπ’ ἐμοί καὶ πάντα ἀποδώσω σοι
verses.transliteration: Pesōn oun ho doulos prosekynei autō legōn Makrothymēson ep’ emoi kai panta apodōsō soi
verses.literal: Then the servant fell on his knees before him Have patience with me he begged and I will pay back everything
verses.literalPt: O servo, pois, prostrando-se, o reverenciava, dizendo: Tem paciência comigo, que te pagarei tudo.

verses.original: Σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἀπέλυσεν αὐτόν καὶ τὸ δάνειον ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Splanchnistheis de ho kyrios tou doulou ekeinou apelysen auton kai to daneion aphēken autō
verses.literal: His master - had compassion on him forgave his debt and released him
verses.literalPt: O senhor teve compaixão daquele servo, deixou-o ir e perdoou-lhe a dívida.

verses.original: Ἐξελθὼν δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος εὗρεν ἕνα τῶν συνδούλων αὐτοῦ ὃς ὤφειλεν αὐτῷ ἑκατὸν δηνάρια καὶ κρατήσας αὐτὸν ἔπνιγεν λέγων Ἀπόδος εἴ τι ὀφείλεις
verses.transliteration: Exelthōn de ho doulos ekeinos heuren hena tōn syndoulōn autou hos ōpheilen autō hekaton dēnaria kai kratēsas auton epnigen legōn Apodos ei ti opheileis
verses.literal: But when that servant went out he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii He grabbed him and began to choke him saying Pay back what you owe me
verses.literalPt: Tendo saído, porém, aquele servo, encontrou um dos seus companheiros que lhe devia cem denários; e, segurando-o, o sufocava, dizendo-lhe: Paga o que me deves.

verses.original: Πεσὼν οὖν ὁ σύνδουλος αὐτοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν λέγων Μακροθύμησον ἐπ’ ἐμοί καὶ ἀποδώσω σοι
verses.transliteration: Pesōn oun ho syndoulos autou parekalei auton legōn Makrothymēson ep’ emoi kai apodōsō soi
verses.literal: So his fellow servant fell down and begged him Have patience with me and I will pay you back
verses.literalPt: Este, caindo-lhe aos pés, implorava: Tem paciência comigo, que te pagarei.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτὸν εἰς φυλακὴν ἕως οὗ ἀποδῷ τὸ ὀφειλόμενον
verses.transliteration: Ho de ouk ēthelen alla apelthōn ebalen auton eis phylakēn heōs hou apodō to opheilomenon
verses.literal: But he refused Instead he went and had the man thrown . . . into prison until . . . he could pay his debt
verses.literalPt: Ele, porém, não o atendeu; mas foi-se embora e mandou conservá-lo preso, até que pagasse a dívida.

verses.original: Ἰδόντες οὖν οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτοῦ τὰ γενόμενα ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα καὶ ἐλθόντες διεσάφησαν τῷ κυρίῳ ἑαυτῶν πάντα τὰ γενόμενα
verses.transliteration: Idontes oun hoi syndouloi autou ta genomena elypēthēsan sphodra kai elthontes diesaphēsan tō kyriō heautōn panta ta genomena
verses.literal: When his fellow servants saw what had happened they were greatly distressed and they went and recounted all of this to their master
verses.literalPt: Vendo, pois, os seus companheiros o que se tinha passado, ficaram muitíssimo tristes e foram contar ao seu senhor tudo o que havia acontecido.

verses.original: Τότε προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ λέγει αὐτῷ Δοῦλε πονηρέ πᾶσαν τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἐκείνην ἀφῆκά σοι ἐπεὶ παρεκάλεσάς με
verses.transliteration: Tote proskalesamenos auton ho kyrios autou legei autō Doule ponēre pasan tēn opheilēn ekeinēn aphēka soi epei parekalesas me
verses.literal: Then the master summoned him and said You wicked servant I forgave all your debt because you begged me
verses.literalPt: Então, o seu senhor, chamando-o, disse-lhe: Servo malvado, eu te perdoei toda aquela dívida, porque me pediste;

verses.original: οὐκ ἔδει καὶ σὲ ἐλεῆσαι τὸν σύνδουλόν σου ὡς κἀγὼ σὲ ἠλέησα
verses.transliteration: ouk edei kai se eleēsai ton syndoulon sou hōs kagō se ēleēsa
verses.literal: Shouldn’t . . . you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you
verses.literalPt: não devias tu também ter compaixão do teu companheiro, como eu tive de ti?

verses.original: καὶ ὀργισθεὶς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν τοῖς βασανισταῖς ἕως οὗ ἀποδῷ πᾶν τὸ ὀφειλόμενον αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: kai orgistheis ho kyrios autou paredōken auton tois basanistais heōs hou apodō pan to opheilomenon autō
verses.literal: In anger his master turned him over . . . to the jailers to be tortured until he should repay all that he owed
verses.literalPt: Irou-se o seu senhor e o entregou aos verdugos, até que pagasse tudo o que lhe devia.

verses.original: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ποιήσει ὑμῖν ἐὰν μὴ ἀφῆτε ἕκαστος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν καρδιῶν ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Houtōs kai ho Patēr mou ho ouranios poiēsei hymin ean mē aphēte hekastos tō adelphō autou apo tōn kardiōn hymōn
verses.literal: That is how My heavenly Father will treat each of you unless . . . you forgive your brother from your heart
verses.literalPt: Assim também meu Pai celestial vos fará, se cada um de vós, do íntimo do coração, não perdoar a seu irmão.
